terms.meaning: Another name for the Sindhu-Saraswati (Indus Valley) Civilization, after Harappa, the first site found.
What the Harappan period is also called, after the alloy its people used.
The name scholars give the Harappan writing on seals. It is still not deciphered.
From the word "Vid", which means knowledge.
A person who recites the hymns of the Rigveda.
The Vedic word for a king, who was helped by the Sabha, Samiti and Vidata.

items.name: How old the civilization is
items.formula: It existed about 5000 years ago and began to decline about 4000 years ago.
items.example: Most sites are in Sindh and Punjab, others in Rajasthan and Gujarat.

items.name: Who dug at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro
items.formula: Dayaram Sahani at Harappa (1920), R. D. Banerjee at Mohenjo-daro (1921).

items.name: Who announced the discovery
items.formula: Sir John Marshall, head of Indian Archaeology, in 1924.
items.example: He published it in the Illustrated London News.

items.name: Early visitors to Harappa
items.example: Alexander Cunningham, first Director General of Archaeology, did small digs.

items.name: Two parts of a Harappan town
items.formula: West: small and raised, called the fort. East: wide and low, called the village.
items.example: Each had a wall of interlocked burnt clay bricks.

items.name: Public bath at Mohenjo-Daro
items.formula: A leak-proof brick tank with stairs on two sides and rooms around it.
items.example: Water probably came from a nearby well and was drained after use.

items.name: Harappan houses
items.formula: Brick, one or two storeys, rooms around a central space, doors to the street but no windows.
items.example: Every house had its own bath.

items.name: Harappan drains
items.formula: Brick drains covered with stone slabs that had holes for cleaning.
items.example: House drains joined the street drains.

items.name: What each Harappan site is known for
items.formula: Lothal: dockyard and sea trade. Dholavira: rain water management. Kalibangan: fire places.

items.name: First villages
items.formula: Burzahom (Kashmir): pit houses against cold and animals.
items.example: Mehrgarh, near the Bolan pass: barley, wheat, sheep and goats.

items.name: Harappan seals
items.formula: The bull and the peepal leaf are the main figures.
items.example: Seals found in Mesopotamia show close trade ties.

items.name: Harappan farming
items.formula: Wheat, barley, pulses and cotton, with oxen to plough.
items.example: Copper for bronze came from Baluchistan and Rajasthan.

items.name: Possible reasons for the decline
items.formula: Rivers drying up or changing course, loss of forests, long floods.
items.example: People moved east and south, but Lothal lasted longer.

items.name: Dates of the Vedic period
items.formula: 1500 BCE to 700 BCE, the start of India's historic period.
items.example: It is divided into the Early (Rigvedic) and Later Vedic periods.

items.name: The Rigveda
items.formula: The first Veda: 1028 Suktas in 10 Mandalas.
items.example: The Purushasukta, in the tenth Mandala, mentions the varnas.

items.name: Society in the Early Vedic period
items.formula: Varna by profession, women equal, widow marriage allowed.
items.example: Main work: animal husbandry and farming.

items.name: Society in the Later Vedic period
items.formula: Caste by birth, women not equal, widow marriage banned.
items.example: Dowry, parda and child marriage began, and farming became the main work.

mistakes.text: Early Vedic varna depended on profession. Fixing it by birth came in the Later Vedic period.
Sahani and Banerjee did the digging. Marshall is the one who announced it to the world.
The Vidata disappeared in the Later Vedic period, while the Sabha and Samiti are named with it in the early one.
